findings: The checksum failure is established and reproduced byte for byte: the release test treated the runner's own logs in test-results\ as release files (runs 1 and 2 report exactly the files the runner had just written).

In both runs windows\Start-Desktop.ps1 did not exit: the runner prints nothing for a host case until the start-up script exits (Run-Logged waits up to 900 s), and the video shows no output 80 s into the case.

The start-up script was still alive when each folder was zipped: Explorer's ZIP omitted exactly the two files that script held open for writing (it cannot open a file another process is writing), while run 2 saw the run-1 file on disk.

No desktop host was running at the start of run 2, so run 1's script never launched one (a headless host started by it would have kept running); the stop happened inside Start-Desktop.ps1 before or at the host launch.

The Milestone 3 script launched the host with a plain Start-Process, i.e. through the Windows shell (ShellExecuteEx). REPRODUCED on a real Windows machine (GitHub-hosted Windows Server 2025, scenario S17): with the release files marked as downloaded (Mark of the Web, as after extracting a downloaded ZIP), the Milestone 3 start-up script, called exactly as the Milestone 3 runner calls it, did not finish within 120 s; its hidden PowerShell owned a dialog of class #32770 titled 'Open File - Security Warning' with visible = 0, and a screenshot taken during the stop shows no dialog on the desktop. The same script on the same files without the mark finished in about 2 s. A process started hidden shows its first window with the hidden flag it was started with, so the prompt can never be seen or answered.
notEstablished: Whether the prompt on the operator PC was 'Open File - Security Warning' or Windows SmartScreen (both are shell prompts for downloaded unsigned programs; both block the Milestone 3 start-up script).
Why the separate RUN-M3-HOST-DIAGNOSTIC.cmd did not work (the file is not available).

rootCause.status: established for the mechanism and reproduced on real Windows; the exact prompt on the operator PC is not observable from the operator's files
rootCause.cause: windows\Start-Desktop.ps1 (Milestone 3) launched the desktop host with a plain Start-Process, i.e. through the Windows shell (ShellExecuteEx). For an unsigned program extracted from a downloaded ZIP (Mark of the Web) the shell asks for confirmation and waits. The Milestone 3 runner had started Start-Desktop.ps1 hidden, and a process started hidden shows its first window hidden, so the prompt was INVISIBLE and could never be answered; the runner waited up to 900 s per start case without output.
